content:
Flu season is getting an early start in the United States. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported Friday, October 23, that seasonal flu activity is increasing in many parts of the country, though it remains low nationally — a climb that began in early September, weeks ahead of the usual November-to-December build.

COVID-19 tells a different story in the same CDC update: activity remains elevated in some regions but is declining nationally, hospitalizations remain low, and are highest among adults 65 and older. Wastewater activity is low nationally but varies by state. RSV activity is very low in most areas, though emergency-department visits among children younger than 5 are low but starting to increase.

Other illnesses are circulating alongside the flu, according to the CDC: Group A strep, rhinovirus and enterovirus, parainfluenza, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and pertussis. In other words, the familiar fall mix of respiratory bugs is already in motion, even before the traditional peak season arrives.

What this means for Webb County readers: no Laredo or Webb County-specific flu figures were available in the CDC's October 23 summary, and Webb Watch 956 will not invent local numbers. The national signal is the story for now — activity rising earlier than usual, from a low base — and local clinics and school nurses are the ones who will see it first if the early climb continues here.

What to watch next: the CDC's weekly updates in the coming weeks will show whether the early rise steepens into an early peak, or levels off. Webb Watch 956 will track the national trend and any Texas-specific data as it is released.

Sources:

  • CDC Respiratory Illnesses Data Channel, reported October 23, 2026
  • WAOV, "Flu numbers climbing," October 24, 2026

title: Flu season starting early: CDC says activity climbing weeks ahead of the usual build
